calls.reason: The only project history is the Replit incident, and that database was recovered and use continued. No study follows a set of projects from good starts to final outcomes, so the frequency implied by 'often' is unestablished.

A Sept 2025 analysis of 518 firsthand accounts found vibe coders knowingly accept flawed code and recognise production and maintenance limits. It cites ~46% distrust in the 2025 Stack Overflow survey. Neither measures a change over time.

The obfuscation and counterfactual studies show performance drops but don't isolate familiarity from difficulty. RealClassEval, posted after the claim, found nearly identical seen and unseen performance, and the claim is hedged ('can be fine').
